title: India Set to Debut Saransh Jain in Colombo as Kuldeep Yadav's Place Comes Under Scrutiny
excerpt: After Manav Suthar's 10-wicket masterclass sealed a 165-run victory in the first Test at Galle, India are weighing changes for the series finale in Colombo starting August 23.
body:
• India are expected to hand a Test debut to 33-year-old off-spinning all-rounder Saransh Jain for the second Test against Sri Lanka, starting August 23 in Colombo
  • Kuldeep Yadav's underwhelming Galle performance has put his place under scrutiny, with Manav Suthar's 10-wicket haul making the case for a spin reshuffle
  • India lead the two-match series 1-0 after a comprehensive 165-run victory in the rain-affected first Test at Galle

India's Dominant Win in Galle

India secured a commanding 165-run victory in the opening Test at Galle on Wednesday, riding a 10-wicket match haul from 24-year-old left-arm spinner Manav Suthar to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.

Devdutt Padikkal's elegant 167 — his maiden Test hundred — powered India to 462 in the first innings after captain Shubman Gill won the toss and opted to bat. KL Rahul contributed 82 before falling just short of a century, while Dhruv Jurel added a breezy 51 lower down the order, according to Reuters.

India bowled Sri Lanka out for 284 in the first innings, led by Suthar who took four wickets. A fighting century from Sonal Dinusha and Niroshan Dickwella's 72 provided resistance, but the hosts could not close the 178-run deficit.

In their second innings, India batted aggressively, with Rishabh Pant smashing 66 to set Sri Lanka a victory target of 372. Suthar then demolished the hosts for 206 in the fourth innings, claiming six wickets — including a three-wicket over that sent Sri Lanka hurtling toward defeat — to finish with match figures of 10 wickets, according to Reuters.

The Saransh Jain Question

With the series already secured, attention has shifted to potential changes for the second Test at the Sinhalese Sports Club in Colombo, starting August 23. The biggest talking point is whether India will hand a debut to Saransh Jain, the 33-year-old Madhya Pradesh off-spinning all-rounder who was called up to replace the injured Washington Sundar.

Jain brings 188 first-class wickets at an average of 27.30 and 2,223 runs at 31.75 from 54 matches — a genuine all-round package. He impressed during the India A tour to Sri Lanka in July, scoring an unbeaten 70 and picking up six wickets in the second four-day game, according to ESPNcricinfo.

If selected, Jain would become India's oldest men's Test debutant in the 21st century, according to Wisden. His selection underlines India's commitment to rewarding consistent domestic performers, even those who have never featured in the IPL.

Kuldeep Under Pressure

The flip side of the team discussion centers on Kuldeep Yadav, whose Galle outing was overshadowed by Suthar's dominance. While Kuldeep was serviceable — and had shown strong form in the warm-up match with a two-wicket haul over 18 overs — Suthar's 10-wicket performance and superior economy raised questions about the need for two frontline spinners alongside Ravindra Jadeja.

Former India cricketer Mohammed Kaif expressed concern about Kuldeep's form ahead of the Colombo Test, while former Test batter Cheteshwar Pujara offered pointed criticism of India's bowling approach during the Galle match, according to NDTV and Indian Express reports.

"Let's spare a thought for Kuldeep. He is someone who always keeps you in the game, irrespective of the conditions."

— Venkatesh Prasad, former India fast bowler

However, former India fast bowler Venkatesh Prasad cautioned against dropping Kuldeep, noting his track record as a match-winner. Multiple pundits have urged captain Gill and coach Gautam Gambhir to retain the wrist spinner for Colombo.

Possible Changes for Colombo

India's likely approach involves bringing in Jain as an additional off-spin option while potentially resting one of the pace bowlers. The Colombo pitch at the SSC is traditionally spin-friendly, which could favor a four-spinner strategy.

The squad for the series, captained by Gill with KL Rahul as vice-captain, also includes Jasprit Bumrah — though the pace spearhead was ruled out of the series due to a knee injury sustained during the England ODIs. Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna led the pace attack in Galle.

For Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, the series carries added significance as part of the ICC World Test Championship 2025-27 cycle. India sit fifth in the WTC standings and need strong results to climb the table after a 2-0 home defeat to South Africa in November.
